title: decision-request v1
description: WHAT A CALLER HANDS TO ONE DECISIONS OPERATION (decisions/Operations.ps1, Invoke-HordeDecision): plain data, one definition per operation, named for it. The command line builds these today; a window and a link between machines are meant to send the same objects later, so nothing here assumes a console, a file or a person typing. A request is checked against its definition before anything is read or written, and one that does not match is refused with what is wrong. The top of this schema describes no value by itself: a caller always names the operation, and the operation table in decisions/Operations.ps1 names the definition. A new operation is a new definition here and a new entry in that table.

id.description: The idempotency id of a request that writes: 32 lowercase hex digits, chosen by the caller and reused unchanged when the same request is sent again.

actor.description: The role label of who is asking. The closed list is the actors of decisions/Rules.ps1; a label it does not hold is refused.

changes.description: The fields to change, schema/decision-question.v1; at least one.

outcome.description: What was done, in plain words.

reason.description: Why it is open again, on one line.

state.description: Which questions: a state name, or all, in any case. Absent means open. The states are the list in decisions/Rules.ps1; any other text is refused there, in words, and no pattern is set here so that the refusal is never a regular expression.

kinds.description: Asks for the table of question kinds. It takes nothing.

say.description: Record words said under a question. They are kept whatever the question's state: under a closed question they are flagged as having arrived after closing, and reopen nothing.

speaker.description: Whose words they are. The closed list is the speakers of decisions/Rules.ps1.

route.description: By what route they arrived. The closed list is the routes of decisions/Rules.ps1, which also says whose words may arrive by each and who may record them: the actor recording a person's chat words is not the speaker.

text.description: The words, verbatim. No pattern is set here, so that a refusal never describes them.

wordingVersion.description: The wording of the question the speaker was looking at. Absent means NOT STATED, and is recorded as that: nothing is guessed. Words typed in the window always state it (the routes of decisions/Rules.ps1 say which routes must).

inbox.description: What others have said, under every question, that the actor has not read yet: oldest first. With mark, the same call records that the actor has now read exactly the messages it is handed, as one record of its own.

mark.description: True to record the messages handed back as read. It needs an id, because it writes. Absent or false reads only, and takes no id.

upTo.description: Only messages whose record is at or before this sequence number are handed back, and marked. A caller that showed a person some messages and then marks them names the last one it showed here, so that one which arrived in between is never marked unseen.
